query:
The group has a norm that plans are confirmed in the chat before being assumed to be happening. Which member does not follow this norm in practice, and what specific pattern of behaviour in the conversations shows they treat it as inapplicable to themselves?

Options:
A. Seb
B. Marcus
C. Priyanka
D. Zara
context:
[1] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:44:00) You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.
[2] (about=Zara, episodic, t6 @2026-01-29T19:49:00) We are not annoyed at you. We just want to know in advance so we can plan accordingly. That is not too much to ask.
[3] (about=Marcus, said_by=Nadia, profile, t12 @2026-02-19T19:55:00) Nadia calls out Marcus for being a vague maybe since October; says group misses him being properly here; Saturday was first time in months he showed up without hedging.
[4] (about=Priyanka, core, t8 @2026-02-05T19:19:00) Proposes celebrating Nadia's news with a low-key dinner at her place instead of going out.
[5] (about=Seb, core, t6 @2026-01-29T19:23:00) Feels guilty about repeatedly cancelling plans due to knee.
[6] (about=Theo, episodic, t14 @2026-02-26T19:40:00) we met because Marcus accidentally walked into the wrong A&E bay and Nadia was the one who had to redirect him. you're right, camping is conservative
[7] (about=Zara, core, t6 @2026-01-29T19:23:00) Group is not annoyed at Seb; just wants advance notice to plan accordingly.
agent_answer:
A. Seb.

The pattern: Seb makes or changes plans without asking/confirming in the chat first. Zara calls this out directly: *“You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.”* She also tells him the group just wants advance notice: *“We just want to know in advance so we can plan accordingly. That is not too much to ask.”* So Seb treats the confirm-before-assuming norm as applying to everyone except himself.

query:
The group has a stated norm that the role of booking and organising rotates — it does not fall to the same person every time. Which members are not following this norm in practice, and what in the conversations reveals their non-compliance?

Options:
A. Nadia and Theo
B. Seb and Marcus
C. Priyanka and Seb
D. Zara and Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:41:00) I am done making all the reservations. I have done it for every single outing this month. Someone else can do it.
[2] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:44:00) You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.
[3] (about=Priyanka, episodic, t6 @2026-01-29T19:54:00) so I'll look into booking it then? the one near Waterloo has good reviews
[4] (about=Seb, core, t10 @2026-02-12T19:41:00) Would have done the booking if asked.
[5] (about=Seb, core, t9 @2026-02-12T19:40:00) Asks who is sorting the escape room booking for Saturday.
[6] (about=Zara, core, t8 @2026-02-05T19:19:00) Corrects Seb: three restaurant things in a row; booking logistics not worth it for a Tuesday-in-January mood.
[7] (about=Zara, core, t10 @2026-02-12T19:41:00) Done making all reservations for every outing this month; someone else can do it.
agent_answer:
From the material, the members **not** following the rotation norm are:

- **Seb** — he asks *“who is sorting the escape room booking for Saturday”* and says *“would have done the booking if asked”* instead of just doing it; Zara calls this out: *“You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.”*
- **Marcus, Nadia, and Theo** — they have **no record** of booking/organising at all, while Zara says she has made **every reservation for every outing this month**.

Priyanka is **following** the norm — she offers to look into the booking. Zara is the one who has been doing all the booking, not the one refusing to rotate.

So the full set of non-compliant people is **Seb, Marcus, Nadia, and Theo** — none of the A–D options matches that complete set.
